items.headline: Hormuz traffic falls to the lowest level since May as Iran prepares a new restricted zone
items.summary: Reuters reports that an average of only 10 commodity ships per day crossed the Strait of Hormuz over the last 10 days, the lowest rate since May, while Iran said it will announce a new restricted zone and revised shipping corridors.
items.whyItMatters: This is a new physical-flow deterioration, not merely rhetoric. It raises the probability of a more persistent oil and freight shock and increases the chance that energy inflation complicates the Fed path.
items.agciSignal: PHYSICAL FLOWS DETERIORATE / RESTRICTED-ZONE RISK UP / KEEP MODERATE ENERGY HEDGE

items.headline: Iran warns that U.S.-linked energy infrastructure in the Gulf is exposed
items.category: Geopolitics / Energy / Real Assets / Sovereign Risk
items.summary: Iranian officials warned that further U.S. attacks could be answered against American-linked oil and gas facilities in the region, while Tehran prepares tighter navigation controls around Hormuz.
items.whyItMatters: The escalation path is broadening from tankers toward fixed energy infrastructure. AGCI treats this as a higher tail risk for Gulf production, refining and logistics, while still separating stated threats from confirmed attacks.
items.agciSignal: ENERGY-INFRASTRUCTURE TAIL RISK UP / THREAT NOT YET A CONFIRMED STRIKE

items.headline: More than $10 billion of tariff refunds are flowing back to S&P 500 companies
items.summary: Barron's reports that S&P 500 companies have begun receiving more than $10 billion of tariff refunds. Most recipients are directing the cash toward reinvestment, customer experience or operating needs rather than distributing the full benefit directly to consumers.
items.whyItMatters: The refunds can temporarily support margins and internal funding, but AGCI does not treat them as recurring operating improvement. Retail and transport names should still be judged on traffic, pricing power, underlying margins and free cash flow.
items.agciSignal: ONE-TIME CASH BENEFIT / DO NOT CAPITALIZE REFUNDS AS STRUCTURAL EARNINGS

items.headline: Greed remains 81 and Valuation 85; Correction regime and EUPHORIA_RISK persist
items.summary: The live AGCI engine remains at Greed 81/100 and Valuation 85/100 with a Correction regime and EUPHORIA_RISK / Capital preservation — Do not chase. The latest market inputs are still dated September 4.
items.whyItMatters: There is no fresh U.S. cash-session observation to justify a manufactured score change. The energy shock is rising while valuation remains extreme, so liquidity and staged entries remain preferable to chasing beta.
items.agciSignal: SCORES UNCHANGED / EXTREME VALUATION / PRESERVE OPTIONALITY
